description.narrative:
Goal: The overall goal of the programme was to contribute to the improvement of Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) of women, adolescents and young people including disadvantaged populations.
Objectives: 1) To strengthen the capacity of the health system to deliver rights based Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn and Adolescent Health services in high maternal mortality burdened regions of Uganda 2) To mobilize social and institutional structures including community, religious and cultural leadership for increased utilization of stigma free SRH/HIV services
Expected outcomes: Increased availability and use of rights based integrated SRH services that meet standards for quality of care and equity in access in high maternal mortality districts and population groups.
Expected outputs 1) Availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality of midwifery and family planning services increased in the 10 targeted districts. 2) The three point access model (health facilities, schools and communities) to provide adolescent and youth friendly services including Sexuality Education in schools is institutionalized and functional in target districts. 3) The Mulago STI/MARPI service delivery structure for key populations is expanded to cover four regional hubs (Mbarara, Gulu, Mbale, Hoima) and KCCA. 4) Existence of transformative, stigmafree and rightsbased HIV prevention and Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights promotion programmes through cultural and religious leaders and male involvement in the target districts.

UNFPA har formulerat ett projekt som ska öka tillgängligheten och användandet av rättighetsbaserade, integrerade SRH tjänster. Tjänsterna ska uppfylla kvalitetsstandard på vård och jämlikhet i tillgången för kvinnor, ungdomar, personer som sex-arbetar och hbt-personer. Projektet ska implementeras i 10 i distrikt med stora behov och som också är belägna i Ugandas post-konflikt områden. Ytterligare fyra hiv-centra inkluderas också i projektet. Effektmålen för projektet är 1) att stärka hälsosystemets kapacitet i att kunna leverera rättighetsbaserade reproduktiva-, mödra-, nyfödda- och ungdomshälsotjänster i geografiska områden med hög mödradödlighet och 2) att mobilisera strukturer, såsom grupper på landsbygden, religiösa och kulturella ledare för att öka användandet av SRH och hiv tjänster fria från stigmatisering.
De personer som direkt gagnas av projektet är befolkningen i de post-konflikt drabbade områdena Acholi och Karamoja, speciellt unga flickor och marginaliserade grupper. Den totala populationen som kommer gagnas av projektet beräknas uppgå till 1 770 224 personer
UNFPA kommer vara ambassadens kontraktspartner och den enhet som är ansvarig för utvecklingen, implementeringen, uppföljningen och rapporteringen av projektet. UNFPA kommer vara ansvariga för projektresultaten och finansieringen. Medel kommer att vidarebefordras till tredje part.

UNFPA has designed an intervention to increase availability and use of rights-based, integrated SRH services that meet standards of quality of care and equity in access for women, young people, sex workers and LGBT persons in 10 high-need districts in post-conflict areas of Uganda (plus 4 HIV hubs). The strategic objectives of the intervention are 1) To strengthen the capacity of the health system to deliver rights-based Reproductive, Maternal, New-born and Adolescent Health services to high maternal mortality burdened regions of the country; and 2) To mobilize institutional structures including community, religious and cultural leadership for increased utilization of stigma-free SRH/HIV services.
The direct beneficiaries in this project are the rights holders in the post-conflict areas of Acholi and Karamoja, including women and young people, especially adolescent girls, and most at risk populations focusing on districts with poor sexual reproductive health indicators (total population 1,770,224).
UNFPA will be Sweden's contracting partner and responsible for development, implementation, monitoring and reporting of the project. UNFPA will also be accountable for project results and finance. Project funds for implementation will be forwarded to partners (almost all of the project oriented funds). Procurement will mainly be handled through the UNFPA system.

UNFPA summarizes the main achievements from the implementation period, starting in November 2015, along the following lines:
- Increased capacities among hospitals and health centres to provide Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CemONC) and Postabortion care (PAC). - Increased numbers of Midwives being able to provide quality care for maternal and newborn health. - Improved access to Family Planning (FP) and Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) information and services. - Improved access to SRH services among young people across 10 districts in Uganda. - Improved access to quality care for most at risk populations (MARPs) and other key populations in marginalized communities across Uganda.
The first achievement is exemplified by an increase among hospitals and health centres to provide CemONC and PAC from 33% in 2015 to 72% in 2018. Additionally, health care facilities showcased an increase from 8% to 96% in providing Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BemONC). Consequently, during the period of implementation, Uganda registered significant improvements on Maternal Mortality Ratio with a decline from 438 deaths per 100.000 live births in 2011 to 336 deaths in 2016. Also, the modern contraceptive prevalence rate increased from 30% in 2011 to 36.3% in 2016. Furthermore, districts with functional Maternal Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) increased to 66% compared from 0% at the baseline study. To achieve this, 138 student midwives were offered full tuition scholarships as a part of this program. Therefore, throughout this program, it has been a strong focus in improving access and provision of quality maternal/midwifery and family planning services while strengthening the health systems and building capacity for CemONC, midwifery, and family planning.
Another major achievement of this program was that 279.912 youth and adolescents were reached with SRHR services at strengthened health facilities across 10 districts in Uganda. To reinforce the capacities among health facilities (HFs) to provide youth friendly services, 174 HFs were equipped to provide youth friendly services through training and mentorship of service providers. Alongside, UNFPA together with partners supported the efforts of Uganda in eliminating preventable maternal deaths and Mother to Child Transmission (EMTCT). As a result, 67% of the 88.025 pregnant women, in comparison to the 47% at the baseline study, managed to deliver from health facilities in 2018. Furthermore, 96.2% of pregnant and lactating mothers in the 10 supported districts were reached with lifelong Anti-retroviral therapy (ART) services, reflecting an increment from 72% at the baseline study. Totally, 492.203 new users were reached with family planning services.
This program supported the finalization of the National Sexuality Education Framework in May 2018 where UNFPA continues to support the Ministry of Education and Sports (MOES), both technically and financially in the roll-out of its implementation. Moreover, UNFPA has functionalized the seven hubs of Kampala, Mbarara, Hoima, Fort Portal, Gulu, Wakiso, and Mbale, which have provided integrated SRH/HIV services to 48.884 MARPS and other key populations. In another effort to have a transformative stigma-free and rights-based SRH/HIV programs through cultural and religious leaders, 10 cultural institutions from across Uganda were assisted to develop institutional positions on SRH/HIV/GBV/FP, including pronouncements in selected areas. This included, among others, the implementation of marriage practices to provide customary marriage certificates only to individuals above 18 years while penalizing those engaging in early marriages.
Despite the significant progress that has been made in reducing infant and child mortality over the past decades, neonatal mortality has remained static at 27 per 1000 live deaths between 2011 and 2016. Besides, there are recurring challenges concerning Reproductive Maternal Newborn Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) where young people (10-24 years) contribute to as high as 41% of all new HIV infections. Alongside, adolescent pregnancy contributes to 28% of all maternal mortality. These challenges coupled with strong socio-cultural norms, poverty, limited access, and lack of accurate information continues to affect mothers, girls, adolescents, and youth disproportionately. Therefore, for future implementation, there is a need of addressing the difficulties in the provision of activities such as family planning due to cultural and traditional practices, specifically in Karamoja, requiring specifically tailored strategies and interventions to be implemented. Also, targeted communities would benefit from scaling-up Empowerment and Livelihoods for Adolescents (ELA) since they have proven to improve access to SRH information and services for girls. Finally, regular engagement and participation of district leaders for accountability and commitment would support the provision of quality services. However, with that being said, UNFPA has through this program contributed to substantial progress when it comes to the improvement of SRHR of women, adolescents, and young people, including disadvantaged populations, documented by an increased availability and use if rights based integrated SRH services.
